Title: Verify that malicious file uploads (e.g., executable files) are rejected during photo upload
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Click the 'Upload' button for any photo type (e.g., 'Order Cloth').
2. In the file picker, select a file with an executable extension (e.g., 'malicious.exe' or 'malicious.php').
3. Confirm the upload.
4. Observe the system response.
5. Repeat steps 1-4 with a file containing a null byte in its name (e.g., 'malicious\0.png').
6. Repeat steps 1-4 with a file containing path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../malicious.png').

Test Data: Files: malicious.exe, malicious.php, malicious\0.png, ../../malicious.png
Expected Result: The system should reject all non-image files with an error message such as 'Only image files are allowed'. The upload should not proceed, and no photo should appear in the preview or be saved to the order.

Title: Verify that oversized image uploads are rejected or handled appropriately
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Click the 'Upload' button for any photo type (e.g., 'Order Cloth').
2. In the file picker, select an image file larger than 10MB.
3. Confirm the upload.
4. Observe the system response.

Test Data: Image file: 15MB sample.jpg
Expected Result: The system should reject the oversized image with an error message such as 'Image size exceeds the maximum allowed limit of 10MB'. The upload should not proceed, and no photo should appear in the preview or be saved to the order.

Title: Verify that base64-encoded image uploads are sanitized and do not allow injection attacks
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Intercept the network request during a legitimate photo upload (e.g., using browser dev tools).
2. Modify the base64 payload in the request to include malicious JavaScript (e.g., `<script>alert('xss')</script>` embedded in the image metadata).
3. Send the modified request.
4. Observe the system response and check if the malicious script executes or is rendered in the UI.

Test Data: Modified base64 payload with embedded script: `<script>alert('xss')</script>`
Expected Result: The system should sanitize the base64 payload and either reject the upload or strip out the malicious script. The photo should either not appear in the preview, or the script should not execute when the photo is displayed.

Title: Verify that photo uploads enforce authentication and authorization
Preconditions: User is not logged in (clear all session and local storage tokens/cookies)
Steps:
1. Navigate directly to the 'Add Photos' step of order creation by entering the URL in the browser.
2. Attempt to upload a photo.
3. Observe the system response.
4. Log in as a different user who does not own the order in progress (if possible).
5. Attempt to upload a photo to the existing order.
6. Observe the system response.

Test Data: Valid image file: sample.png
Expected Result: The system should redirect the unauthenticated user to the login page or display an 'Unauthorized' error. For the logged-in user, the system should either prevent access to the order or display an 'Access Denied' error.

Title: Verify that server-side photo URLs are not exposed to unauthorized users

Steps:

2. Note the server-side photo URLs displayed (if any).
3. Log out as User A.
4. Log in as User B.
5. Attempt to access the photo URLs noted in step 2 by entering them directly in the browser.
6. Observe the system response.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The system should prevent User B from accessing the photo URLs directly. The browser should display an 'Access Denied' error or redirect to the login page.

5. Re-inspect the session storage to ensure all order-related data is cleared.

Test Data: N/A

Title: Verify that photo upload API enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Add Photos' step of order creation with a valid customer and item selected
Steps:
1. Click the 'Upload' button for any photo type (e.g., 'Order Cloth').
2. Select a valid image file and confirm the upload.
3. Immediately attempt to upload the same file 10 times in rapid succession (e.g., using a script or rapid clicks).
4. Observe the system response after the first few uploads.

Test Data: Valid image file: sample.png
Expected Result: The system should allow the first few uploads but eventually throttle or block further requests with an error message such as 'Too many requests. Please try again later.'

Title: Verify that order confirmation does not expose sensitive data in error messages or logs
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached the 'Confirm Order' step with photos uploaded
Steps:
1. Proceed to the 'Confirm Order' step.
2. Intercept the network request during order submission (e.g., using browser dev tools).
3. Modify the request payload to include invalid or malicious data (e.g., negative makingCharge, SQL injection in deliveryDate).
4. Send the modified request.
5. Observe the system response and any error messages displayed.
6. Check the browser console and network logs for any sensitive data exposure (e.g., tokens, raw photo URLs, customer PII).

Test Data: Modified payload: { makingCharge: -1000, deliveryDate: "2023-01-01'; DROP TABLE orders;--" }
Expected Result: The system should reject the invalid payload with a generic error message such as 'Invalid order data. Please try again.' No sensitive data (e.g., tokens, photo URLs, customer PII) should be exposed in error messages or logs.

Title: Verify that authentication tokens are securely handled and not exposed in URLs or logs
Preconditions: User is logged in and has reached any step of order creation
Steps:
1. Open the browser's developer tools and inspect the network tab.
2. Navigate through the order creation steps (e.g., 'Add Photos', 'Confirm Order').
3. Check all network requests for the presence of authentication tokens in URLs, headers, or request payloads.
4. Observe if tokens are logged in the browser console or network tab.
5. Log out of the application and verify that tokens are cleared from storage and cookies.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: Authentication tokens should never appear in URLs or be logged in the browser console. Tokens should be sent securely in request headers (e.g., Authorization: Bearer <token>). After logout, all tokens should be cleared from session storage, local storage, and cookies.

Title: Verify that order IDs are not predictable or susceptible to insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
Section: Order Creation - Order ID Generation Security
Preconditions: User is logged in and has completed an order
Steps:
1. Complete an order and note the generated order ID displayed on the success page.
2. Log out and log in as a different user.
3. Manually modify the URL to access the success page of the first user's order (e.g., by incrementing or decrementing the order ID in the URL).
4. Observe the system response.
5. Repeat step 3 with a random order ID not associated with any user.

Test Data: N/A
Expected Result: The system should prevent access to order details for orders not owned by the logged-in user. The user should see an 'Access Denied' error or be redirected to a safe page (e.g., dashboard).
